findings.title: Concurrent delete still causes NPE in getSubGroupsStream overloads
findings.body: This PR acknowledges that modelSupplier.get() can return null when the group was deleted concurrently and makes getSubGroupsCount null-safe. The three getSubGroupsStream overloads in the same file still do modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) without any null check. If the group disappears between cache lookup and DB lookup they throw NullPointerException, the exact failure this PR claims to fix. Consequence is 500 errors remain for concurrent list/search of subgroups. They need the same null handling as getSubGroupsCount, e.g. return Stream.empty().

findings.title: Background reader thread never joined and flag not set on failure
findings.body: The new test starts a background thread that loops calling the admin API until deletedAll becomes true, deletes groups on the main thread, then immediately asserts without joining. If any delete throws, deletedAll.set(true) is skipped and the reader spins forever, leaking a thread. Even on success the assert can run while a read is still in-flight, so later exceptions are missed and the still-running tight loop with no sleep hammers the server and can interfere with subsequent tests. Consequence is hangs, leaks, flaky results and missed regressions. Store the Thread, set the flag in finally, join with timeout, and throttle the loop.

findings.title: Concurrency test never requests subgroup counts so it does not cover the fix
findings.body: The fixed method is GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount, which is only invoked when subgroup counts are requested via GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount when subGroupsCount is true. The new test only calls groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true), i.e. brief representation without subgroup counts. Because it never enables that path it exercises neither the old NullPointerException nor the new null handling, so it would pass with or without the fix and gives false confidence. The concurrent reads must request subgroup counts/hierarchy to be a valid regression test.
